channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Building Surrounded by Police Amid Judicial Dispute
item.description: Police surrounded Poland's Constitutional Tribunal building in Warsaw after a judge suspended its president and vice-president. The judge cited obstruction of justice. The tribunal's website claims the court was "hijacked," while police stated they were responding to a potential threat. Protesters gathered, and three arrests were made.

item.title: Kazakhstan Seizes Nearly 12 Kilograms of Drugs in Caspian Sea Operations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Border Service has seized approximately 11.5 kilograms of narcotics during operations in the Caspian Sea. The agency also confiscated 88 kilometers of illegal fishing gear and released 2,337 sturgeon and other fish back into their natural habitat. Fines totaling over 4.5 million tenge were imposed.

item.title: MP: New Draft of Bishkek's General Plan Not Yet Published
item.description: A Member of Parliament stated that while the Cabinet of Ministers has amended Bishkek's General Plan until 2050, the updated master drawing has not been published. The document, which defines the capital's functional zones, was published without the revised drawing, and public discussion information is missing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Build 112 New Schools and 40 Hospitals by 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to construct 112 new schools and 40 hospitals by 2027 as part of ongoing social infrastructure improvements. The Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh highlighted significant development under President Sadyr Japarov, noting the construction of 700 educational facilities and 500 factories in the past five years.

item.title: CSTO Operation 'Channel - Caspian Beacon' Seizes Drugs, Weapons, and Crypto
item.description: The CSTO's anti-narcotics operation 'Channel - Caspian Beacon' concluded, targeting drug trafficking and criminal groups. Authorities seized narcotics, psychotropic substances, weapons, and ammunition. The operation also uncovered cryptocurrency schemes and identified online platforms used for drug propaganda. It involved law enforcement, border, and customs agencies from CSTO member states, along with Iran and China.

item.title: Afghanistan's Taliban Spokesperson: Pakistan Unwilling to Resolve Tensions Through Dialogue
item.description: Zabihullah Mujahid, spokesperson for Afghanistan's Islamic Emirate, stated that Kabul's efforts to resolve tensions with Pakistan through dialogue have failed. He attributed the lack of progress to Pakistan's 'wrong policies,' asserting that Islamabad shows little willingness for peaceful negotiations. Mujahid reiterated Afghanistan's commitment to resolving disputes diplomatically, despite ongoing bilateral tensions.

item.title: Badakhshan Governor Urges Youth to Reject Opposition and Foster National Unity
item.description: Badakhshan Governor Rahmatullah Najib called on Afghan youth to reject foreign propaganda and opposition groups, emphasizing national unity and an end to violence. He described the current system as a shared home for all Afghans and warned against armed activities not sanctioned as legitimate jihad.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Select Military Food Service Companies via Tender for 2027-2028
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense plans to hold a state tender to select companies that will provide catering services for military personnel in 2027-2028. The tender process will be conducted through the State Procurement Center, with details to be announced on the Kazakhstan State Procurement Web Portal.

item.title: Taliban Fighter Killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Transferred to Maidan Wardak
item.description: Local sources in Maidan Wardak report that the body of a Taliban fighter, identified as Matiullah Aziz, who was killed in clashes with Pakistani forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, has been transferred to the province. The incident occurred two days prior to the report.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Claims Pakistan Unprepared for Peaceful Dispute Resolution
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid stated that Pakistan is not adequately prepared to resolve disputes with the Taliban peacefully. Despite dialogue and mediation efforts, tensions remain high. Mujahid cited Pakistan's "wrong policies" as an obstacle, asserting the Taliban initiated no problems and remain committed to negotiation.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Russia Observer Status in Turkic States Organization
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed considering Russia's participation in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) as an observer or through an "OTS+" format. This initiative, made during the 13th OTS summit in Ankara, aims to leverage historical ties and strengthen Eurasian cooperation without opposing integration processes.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Singapore to Enhance Technical Cooperation in Civil Aviation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Aviation Administration (KAA) and Singapore's Civil Aviation Authority (CAAS) signed a Statement of Intent to expand technical partnership, covering flight safety, risk-based oversight, personnel training, and sustainable development. This agreement broadens cooperation beyond existing training programs, with a new MoU planned for 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan Mandates Fortification of Flour and Iodization of Salt from September
item.description: Starting September 1st, Tajikistan will require premium and first-grade wheat flour intended for the domestic market to be sold only in fortified form. The new regulations also mandate the iodization of salt. These measures aim to improve public health and nutrition across the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Holds Seminar on Increasing Local Budget Revenues and Reducing Shadow Economy
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan's Committee on Budget and Economic Issues organized a seminar for local deputies on enhancing local budget revenues and curbing the shadow economy. Discussions focused on regional financial autonomy, tax administration improvements, and strengthening parliamentary oversight.

item.title: Illegally Constructed Emergency Ministry Building Demolished at Baitik Weather Station
item.description: An illegally constructed building belonging to the Ministry of Emergency Situations has been demolished at the Baitik weather station in Kyrgyzstan. The structure was built within the water protection zone of the Ala-Archa River. The former minister of emergency situations was prosecuted, and the state's losses were compensated.

item.title: Taliban to Demolish Two Kandahar Commercial Centers, Shopkeepers Seek Compensation
item.description: The Taliban have ordered the demolition of two commercial centers, Mirwais and Roshan, in Kandahar's Arg Bazaar. Shopkeepers, who have invested approximately 400 million afghanis, face unemployment and economic damage. They are demanding compensation and a suitable relocation before the demolition proceeds.

item.title: Large Drug Haul Seized from Fishing Boat in Caspian Sea
item.description: During special operations in the Caspian Sea in October, 126 offenders were detained and 44 small watercraft were confiscated. The National Security Committee reported that 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 km of poaching nets were found. Over 2,337 sturgeon and other fish were released back into their natural habitat.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Raise Minimum Wage, Invest Trillions in Infrastructure
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced a minimum wage increase to 110,000 tenge and the allocation of 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund for infrastructure projects. Kazakhstan aims for energy self-sufficiency by 2029. Micro and small businesses will be exempt from inspections for three years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Success Not Driven by Russia, Says National Bank Head
item.description: International investors view Kyrgyzstan's close ties with Russia as a risk due to sanctions. National Bank Chairman Almaz Baketaev stated that while Russia is a partner, it's not the main driver of Kyrgyzstan's economic success. Sanctions against Russia have provided Kyrgyzstan with an economic boost and increased cross-border trade.

item.title: Israel's Election Results Leave Coalition Government Formation Uncertain
item.description: Israel's recent election results have created an unclear path to forming a coalition government. No single bloc secured the necessary 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats, the opposition bloc 48, and the Arab bloc 19, necessitating complex coalition negotiations or potential new elections.

item.title: Iran's Supreme Leader Orders Immediate Response to Any Threat
item.description: Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, has instructed the armed forces to respond immediately and without geographical limitations to any potential threat. He stated that if enemies initiate military or terrorist attacks again, Iran's armed forces and people will determine the end of such actions. Khamenei emphasized strengthening military intelligence and defense capabilities.

item.title: Apple Regains Title of World's Most Valuable Company with $5.03 Trillion Valuation
item.description: Apple has reclaimed its position as the world's most valuable company, with its market capitalization reaching $5.03 trillion by the end of October. This surpasses chip developer Nvidia, now second at $4.93 trillion. Investor confidence in AI appears to favor Apple's stock as a more stable investment.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Awards Winners of "Zakovat-Gambit" Chess Tournament
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, presented awards at the fifth "Zakovat-Gambit" chess tournament. This year's competition attracted nearly 6,000 participants, double last year's figure, with 633 female participants.

item.title: Suspected fraudster arrested in Shymkent over 4 billion tenge scam
item.description: A 45-year-old man, wanted internationally for fraud, has been arrested in Shymkent. He is suspected of defrauding nearly 300 investors of over 4 billion tenge by allegedly collecting funds for an apartment complex in Astana, built without permits. The suspect is in temporary detention.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan plans to issue yuan-denominated bonds in 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to issue sovereign bonds in Chinese yuan in 2027, according to National Bank Chairman Almaz Baketaev. The government is considering listing them on the Hong Kong or Shanghai stock exchanges. This move reflects the yuan's growing role in Kyrgyzstan's economy and trade ties with China.

item.title: Tokayev proposes state commission to oversee 'People's Construction' program
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed establishing a state commission to strictly control the spending of budget funds for the 'Khalyktyk Kurylys' ('People's Construction') program. Announced on October 28, the program aims to build approximately 70 facilities, including hospitals and schools, by 2029, with funding from the National Fund.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Criminal Liability for Stalking from September 2025
item.description: Kazakhstan introduced criminal liability for stalking on September 16, 2025. As of June 9, 2026, 83 criminal cases related to stalking have been sent to court. Almaty registered 24 applications concerning stalking from early 2026 to the end of April.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Claims Over 5,000 Lives, WHO Reports
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in 5,026 confirmed deaths and 10,351 infections. Currently, 1,101 individuals are undergoing treatment or quarantine, while 2,788 have recovered. Experts suggest the actual death toll may be higher due to undetected spread.

item.title: WHO Warns of Global Spread of New 'Ultramutant' Coronavirus Variant PJ.2.1
item.description: The World Health Organization warns of increased risks from the new coronavirus variant PJ.2.1, an 'ultramutant' first detected in Canada in May 2026. While it has many mutations, there's no confirmation it causes more severe illness. It is actively circulating in the US, Canada, and Europe.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains 125 Violators and 44 Vessels in Caspian Sea During October
item.description: Kazakhstan's border guards detained 126 offenders and 44 small vessels in the Caspian Sea during October. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 km of illegal fishing gear. Over 2,300 fish were released back into their natural habitat, and fines totaling over 4.5 million tenge were imposed.

item.title: Kazakh Diplomat Dusen Kaseinov Honored with Alisher Navoi International Prize
item.description: Kazakh statesman, diplomat, and musician Professor Dusen Kaseinov has been awarded the Alisher Navoi International Prize for his contributions to the unity of the Turkic world. The award recognizes his significant efforts in strengthening cultural ties and promoting Turkic culture globally. Kaseinov previously led the International Organization of Turkic Culture (TURKSOY) for 14 years.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Diplomatic Relations with All UN Member States
item.description: Kazakhstan has established diplomatic relations with Nauru, its 195th UN member state. This marks the completion of Kazakhstan's process of establishing diplomatic ties with all UN member nations, a significant milestone for its diplomacy. Discussions focused on political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth Approaches Uzbekistan's, Outpacing in Average Wages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is emerging as a regional economic leader, with its GDP growing nearly 50% in five years under President Japarov. The country is undertaking major infrastructure projects and is now catching up to Uzbekistan in some economic indicators, having already surpassed it in average wages.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Allocate 6.5 Trillion Tenge from National Fund for Infrastructure
item.description: Kazakhstan plans an unprecedented infrastructure modernization, allocating approximately 6.5 trillion tenge from the National Fund by the end of 2029. President Tokayev proposed naming this initiative 'People's Construction'. The funds will be used for social, transport, and engineering facilities nationwide.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish State Commission to Oversee 'People's Construction' Program
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the creation of a state commission to strictly monitor the spending of budget funds during the implementation of the 'People's Construction' program. The commission will include government officials, parliament members, and public figures.

item.title: Police Arrest Man in Shymkent for Alleged Housing Scam in Astana
item.description: Police in Astana have arrested a 45-year-old man in Shymkent who was internationally wanted for an alleged housing scam. The suspect, along with accomplices, allegedly defrauded citizens by attracting funds for an apartment complex construction without proper permits or state expert review. Over 292 investors were affected, with total damages exceeding 4 billion tenge.

item.title: WHO Director-General Praises Kazakhstan's Commitment to "Health for All"
item.description: The Director-General of the World Health Organization, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, has highly praised Kazakhstan's attention to public health and well-being. He highlighted President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's commitment to increasing the salaries of 77,000 healthcare workers and investing in primary healthcare. Ghebreyesus noted Kazakhstan's role in the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration and its continued practical implementation of its principles.

item.title: Taliban Claim Pakistan Unwilling to Pursue Peaceful Resolution of Tensions
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid stated that the group has made efforts for a peaceful resolution of tensions with Pakistan, but these have been unsuccessful. He asserted that Pakistan is unwilling to adopt a peaceful approach. Mujahid claimed the Taliban are in a defensive position and not the initiators of the conflict, which stems from Pakistan's concerns over militant groups operating from Afghan soil.

item.title: WHO Praises Kazakhstan's Plan to Increase Healthcare Worker Salaries
item.description: The World Health Organization has endorsed Kazakhstan's initiative to raise salaries for 77,000 healthcare professionals. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus expressed support for President Tokayev's commitment to investing in primary healthcare and prioritizing public well-being. This move aligns with the global 'Health for All' vision, a principle established by the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Announces Creation of State Commission for 'People's Construction' Oversight
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has announced the establishment of a state commission tasked with overseeing the 'People's Construction' project. This initiative aims to ensure proper management and accountability for the development project, though further details on the commission's specific mandate were not immediately provided.
